destination.name: Arnhem Land
destination.tagline: Beaches, laterite cliffs and Yolngu art on the Gove Peninsula in north-east Arnhem Land.
destination.description: The Gove Peninsula sits at the north-eastern corner of Arnhem Land, about 600 km from Darwin on Yolngu country. Nhulunbuy is the base for white-sand beaches, rust-red cliffs and a sandspit walk to East Woody Island, while Yirrkala, 19 km away, is home to the Buku-Larrnggay Mulka art centre and museum. Bremer Island lies offshore for day trips by boat. Most of the land is Aboriginal-owned, so visits to its recreation areas need a permit.
whyVisit: Watch the tide at East Woody Island

goodToKnow.title: Dhimurru permit needed
goodToKnow.detail: East Woody, Cape Wirrawoi, Rainbow Cliffs and Macassan Beach need a Dhimurru Visitor Access Permit: $30 per adult for a day.

goodToKnow.title: Fly in or drive
goodToKnow.detail: Airnorth flies from Darwin to Gove. The Central Arnhem Road is unsealed, a dry-season route, and needs a separate transit permit.

goodToKnow.title: Boat trips follow the tides
goodToKnow.detail: Bremer Island day trips leave Nhulunbuy at tide-dependent times; one operator runs them Wednesday to Sunday, April to October.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: The Dry season, {months}, brings sunny days and cooler nights and opens the Central Arnhem Road; the Wet, November to April, means storms and cyclone risk.
